errors.evidence: The y-axis is a logarithmic scale and cannot start at 0. The scale shown starts at 10^0, which is 1.

errors.text_span: For each year, there is a group of six bars, one for each language
errors.evidence: This is not true for all years. For example, from 2012 to 2015, only one bar (for English) is shown each year.

errors.text_span: The shortest bar, representing the number of Arabic datasets in 2012, has an approximate value of 1
errors.evidence: The chart does not show a bar for Arabic datasets in 2012. The only bar present in 2012 is for English.

errors.text_span: the tallest bar for English datasets in 2022 has an approximate value of 100
errors.evidence: The tallest bar for English datasets is in 2021, not 2022. The value for English in 2022 is much lower, approximately 13, not 100.

errors.text_span: The bars representing “All other” consistently have a value between 1 and 10 across all years
errors.evidence: This is incorrect. For several years, the value for 'All other' is significantly higher than 10 (e.g., ~20 in 2018, ~45 in 2020, ~40 in 2021).

errors.text_span: English datasets show a general increase throughout the time series
errors.evidence: This is an over-simplification that omits a key feature of the trend. While the value for English increases until 2021, it experiences a very sharp drop in 2022.

errors.text_span: No bars are visually emphasized with shading, bolding, or annotations.
errors.evidence: This statement is incorrect. The bars for the year 2022 are clearly de-emphasized with a lighter shading or transparency compared to the bars for all other years.
